title: GPU pool pacing: implement admission-score smoothing and model-downgrade policy
creator: Asha Mehta
summary: Follow-up for hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event on 2026-02-10. Root cause analysis identified a confluence of long-tail KV cache pollution from a training-like tenant, aggressive prefill behavior for a subset of small-tenants, and a brittle autoscaler hysteresis that delayed new-slot allocation. The incident manifested as sustained queue buildup, P95/P99 latency degradation, and tenant throttling that persisted despite surge capacity. This ticket tracks the engineering work to harden admission and autoscaling behavior via admission score smoothing, deferred-prefill gating, tenant pacing tokens, and an automated model-downgrade fallback path for heavy requests.
action_items: Implement admission-score smoothing (exponential moving average over 30s) to avoid sharp admission oscillations - owner: Diego - estimate 2
Add deferred-prefill gating: detect prefill-heavy tenants and route prefill to low-priority burst lanes with token-based pacing - owner: Priya Rao - estimate 3
Model-downgrade policy: automatic transparent swap to compatible quantized model variant when queue depth > threshold - owner: Yun Park - estimate 3
Autoscaler hysteresis reduction: tune scale-up fast-path for slot-starvation and add predictive priming ramp based on 1m growth signal - owner: SRE team (Jamal) - estimate 2
Create tenant-fairness telemetry dashboard (queue-depth by tenant/class, admission-score distribution, eviction events) and add alerts - owner: Observability (Lina) - estimate 2
Add Chaos/Load test: synthetic long-tail KV pollution scenario in staging to validate mitigations - owner: QA (Marco) - estimate 2
decision_log: 2026-02-16: Decided to prioritize admission smoothing + deferred-prefill over immediate global throttle because throttles had high customer impact and masked root cause.
2026-02-18: Chose 30s EMA window after comparing 10s, 30s, 60s in simulation; 30s smooths spikes without delaying response to sustained surges.
2026-02-20: Approved model-downgrade as first-line fallback (only for compatible quantized variants) to preserve latency SLOs rather than evicting tenants.
2026-02-25: Rejected full prefix-cache eviction as initial mitigation due to risk of cold-cache amplification; opted for tenant-level pacing instead.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha Mehta: Initial incident report posted. Immediate mitigation applied: temporary tenant caps and emergency prewarm. Postmortem scheduled.
2026-02-13 - Diego Alvarez: Reproduced queue amplification in local load test by replaying tenant traces with KV cache thrash. Identified prefill pattern for small tenants as catalyst.
2026-02-17 - Priya Rao: Prototyped deferred-prefill gating in staging; initial results show 40% reduction in queue length under mixed-workload replay.
2026-02-23 - Yun Park: Implemented a prototype model-downgrade switch in the routing layer; needs canary validation for fallthrough compatibility.
2026-03-01 - Jamal (SRE): Rolled out autoscaler hysteresis tweak to two pools; observed faster slot priming with controlled oscillation. Monitoring remains active.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Smoothing admission scores reduces sensitivity to short bursts and may delay scaling triggers in some pathological ramps; we mitigate this by pairing smoothing with a fast-path growth detector. Model-downgrade improves latency but may slightly reduce output quality for affected requests; downgrade is restricted to compatible quantized variants and opt-out is provided per-tenant for enterprise customers.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for admission smoothing math and invariants. 2) End-to-end staging replay with mixed tenant profiles including KV thrashers. 3) Canary rollout to 5% of pools with circuit breaker to revert. 4) Synthetic fault injection for autoscaler failures.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flags. 2) Canary to isolated GPU pools (5%). 3) Monitor queue-length, P99 latency, eviction_count, and tenant error rates for 24h. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with rollback on predefined thresholds.
success_metrics: Reduce median queue length during surge by >=50% vs baseline; P99 latency back to pre-incident baseline within 15 minutes of surge start; fewer than 2 customer-facing errors per 10k requests during canary.
